narrative.overview: This is not an app that reports on a strategy; it is a device that takes readings of one. A bench instrument has a face, not a home page. It shows a value, the conditions the value was taken under, and how much the value is worth — and it does not editorialise about any of them. The reader is exactly one person, opening it once a day after IDX closes. What they cannot hold in their head is which numbers have earned trust, so the interface carries that instead: every figure is rendered next to its evidence status, in the same visual weight as the figure. Futurism here is carried by precision — tabular figures, hairline rules, one scarce signal colour — not by effects.
keyCharacteristics: Mono-forward: the monospace face runs the interface; the proportional face is reserved for prose
Tables and hairline rules instead of cards; nothing is boxed that is not genuinely a separate object
One signal colour, budgeted under 5% of the surface
Every figure carries an evidence glyph, and every direction carries a sign
Density over chunking: one expert reader, one screen, once a day

rules.name: The Scarce Signal Rule
rules.body: Calibration Chartreuse covers under 5% of any screen. If a second element wants it, one of them is wrong. Its rarity is the entire reason it means something.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: No fact may be encoded in hue alone. Direction carries a sign and a glyph; evidence status carries a glyph; regime carries a word. Strip the colour and the page must still be readable.

rules.name: The Measured-Not-Assumed Rule
rules.body: Every text-on-background pair ships only after its contrast ratio is computed. The palette this replaced used zinc-500/600/700 for labels, measuring 4.12 / 2.57 / 1.91:1 on zinc-950 — two of the three failed AA outright.

rules.name: The Numbers-Are-The-Typography Rule
rules.body: The type scale spans 11px to 22px, deliberately shallow. Emphasis comes from alignment, tabular figures, and colour budget, not from size. If a value needs to be bigger to be noticed, the layout is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Section headings are a title and a rule that runs to the edge. No small uppercase tracked kicker above them, ever.

rules.name: The Flat Face Rule
rules.body: box-shadow is prohibited. If an element needs to separate from its neighbour, give it a 1px rule. If it needs to separate from the page, give it a tonal step. There is no third option.

rules.name: The Glow Audit
rules.body: If you find yourself reaching for a coloured blur to make something feel important, the information hierarchy has failed and the blur is covering for it.

dos: Do compute the contrast ratio of every new text/background pair before shipping it. AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large) is the floor, not the target.
Do pair every colour-encoded fact with a sign, glyph, or word.
Do use U+2212 for negative numbers, not a hyphen. It shares the width of a tabular digit.
Do format numbers Indonesian-style: '.' for thousands, ',' for decimals.
Do separate peers with a 1px rule and sections with rule-hi.
Do keep prose under 70ch and set it in Plex Sans. Everything else is Plex Mono.
Do let motion report a state change and nothing else.
Do give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce path.
donts: Don't use gradients or glow: no gradient surfaces, no blurred colour orbs, no box-shadow glows, no gradient wordmark, no background-clip: text.
Don't put an uppercase tracked eyebrow above every section.
Don't build uniform card grids, and never a card inside a card.
Don't reach for neon-on-black cyber terminal or glassmorphism.
Don't build a hero metric: giant number, small label, supporting stats, accent gradient.
Don't use a coloured border-left wider than 1px as a decorative stripe.
Don't spend the signal colour on decoration.
Don't hide a failed result. Retired strategies stay on screen marked ○.
